rows: Backup and restore
Several hours to a few days
A few hours, up to the last successful backup
Pilot light
A few minutes to several hours
Depends on how often data is synchronized
Warm standby
A few minutes to hours
Up to the last few minutes or hours
Hot site or multi-site
Almost immediate, often a few minutes
Usually a few seconds

sysd-reliab-097.caption: Each pairing trades something away: manual switching, stale reads or unpredictable writes.
rows: Primary-backup
The backup stands by and receives replicated data
Switching is manual and the idle backup may waste hardware
Primary-secondary
The secondary can serve reads to balance load
Replication latency can make its reads inconsistent
Primary-primary
Both nodes handle reads and writes and replicate to each other
The same product updated on both can end up in an unpredictable state

sysd-reliab-221.caption: Three ways to forward a packet, and what each one costs.
rows: Network address translation
The balancer rewrites addresses
A tracking-table entry per connection; no stateless fallback
Change the MAC address
The backend sees the original IPs and replies directly
All balancers and backends in one broadcast domain
Encapsulation
The packet is wrapped in a GRE-encapsulated IP packet
24 bytes of overhead that may exceed the MTU

sysd-reliab-219.caption: Follow the numbered steps from the DNS lookup to the assembled page.
rows: DNS
Google's DNS server consults GSLB, which picks the frontend IP address returned to the user
Google Frontend
A reverse proxy terminates the TCP connection and looks up the service
GSLB
It finds an available service frontend, which receives an RPC with the HTTP request
Service frontend
It builds a protobuf request and asks GSLB for an unloaded backend
Backend
It reads Bigtable, and the reply travels back
Service frontend
It assembles the HTML

sysd-reliab-187.caption: Incident frameworks follow these six stages in order.
sysd-reliab-187.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Detection] --> B[Classification]
B --> C[Response coordination]
C --> D[Containment]
D --> E[Recovery]
E --> F[Post-incident review]

sysd-reliab-186.caption: Each tier up the table keeps data fresher and automates more of recovery.
rows: No off-site data or recovery plan, so recovery may be impossible
Off-site backups but no systems to restore them on; days to weeks of data lost
A hot site to restore tape backups; hours to days of data recreated
Electronic vaulting of mission-critical data, more current than shipped tapes
Disk-based point-in-time copies for fresher data and faster recovery
Data kept consistent between production and recovery data centers
Data kept current with little or no loss, without relying on applications
Automated application recovery, faster and more reliable than manual procedures
